entries.title: Judges 1:1
segments: However great may have been their past successes, the people of God should not rest till fully triumphant over all their foes.

entries.title: Judges 1:3
segments: The union of all classes of pious men in doing good, is greatly promotive of success.

entries.title: Judges 1:4
segments: Bezek; a place in the territory of Judah.

entries.title: Judges 1:5
segments: Adoni-bezek; the lord or king of Bezek.

entries.title: Judges 1:6
segments: Pride and cruelty are forerunners of disaster; and the peculiar sins of men may often be read in their punishment.

entries.title: Judges 1:7
segments:
Threescore and ten; these seventy kings were evidently petty princes, ruling each over a small territory. 
 
A true conviction of the evil of sin will lead all who suffer to feel that their punishment is just.

entries.title: Judges 1:9
segments: The south; the south part of Canaan.

entries.title: Judges 1:10
segments: Hebron; a city twenty miles south of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Judges 1:11
segments: Debir;

entries.title: Judges 1:14
segments: A wise and affectionate wife wishes the temporal propserity as well as the eternal good of her husband, and will use all suitable means to promote it.

entries.title: Judges 1:15
segments: A south land;

Jos 15.16-19. 
 
A wise and affectionate father will take great pleasure in complying, as far as may be consistent, with the requests of his children.

entries.title: Judges 1:16
segments: The Kenite; Jethro.
Arad; a city on the south border of Canaan.

entries.title: Judges 1:17
segments:
Zephath; a place near the south part of Judah. 
 
  Hormah; that is, utter destruction.

entries.title: Judges 1:18
segments: Gaza--Ashkelon--and Edron; cities of the Philistines.

entries.title: Judges 1:19
segments:
Could not; because, terrified by the chariots, they did not trust in God and use the proper means. 
 
Viewing difficulties with an eye of sense only, men often despond, when, should they use proper means in dependence on God, he would render them successful.

entries.title: Judges 1:21
segments: Jerusalem; this city was on the border between Judah and Benjamin, though in the division of the land it was assigned to the latter tribe.

Love of ease, and aversion to great and self-denying efforts, often keep men from receiving the variety and fulness of good which they might otherwise obtain, and leave them to suffer much evil which they might otherwise avoid.

entries.title: Judges 1:22
segments: House of Joseph; that is, the tribe of Ephraim and the half-tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan, though what is here said seems to pertain only to the territory of Ephraim.

entries.title: Judges 1:23
segments:
Descry; examine and ascertain the state of the city. 
 
  Bethel; a place north of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Judges 1:25
segments: Assisting the people of God in doing his will, may be the means of delivering us from many trials and bringing on us great blessings.

entries.title: Judges 1:27
segments:
Beth-shean; a place in the valley of the Jordan near the east end of the valley of Jezreel. 
 
  Taanach; on the south border of the plain of Esdraelon. 
 
  Dor; on the sea, south of Carmel. 
 
  Megiddo; near the Kishon.

entries.title: Judges 1:29
segments:
Gezer; north-west of Jerusalem. 
 
vv 29-33. 
 
Towns within the bounds of the tribes, in connection with whose names they are mentioned.

entries.title: Judges 1:34
segments: The valley; the plain bordering on the Mediterranean, where the Amorites had chariots of iron.  Compare

. 
 
When men neglect their duty, they may expect to meet with trouble; and if they are not led to repentance and reformation, their troubles will never end.

entries.title: Judges 1:35
segments:
Mount Heres; the mountainous regions about Dor. 
 
  Ajalon; a place between Jerusalem and Ekron.
The house of Joseph; his descendents.

entries.title: Judges 1:36
segments:
The Amorites; these stand here for the Canaanites generally. 
 
  Akrabbim; a line of hills running across the valley about eight miles south of the Dead sea, here mentioned as the southern border of Palestine. 
 
  The rock; probably Petra, in the mountains of Edom. 
 
  Upward; northward.
